summary: The note traces the origins of Microsoft Windows, stating that Bill Gates announced it on November 10, 1983. It describes Windows as a graphical user interface built for MS-DOS, which had been introduced a couple of years earlier. It also notes that during the 1990s the product line grew from an operating environment into a complete modern operating system across two development lines with separate codebases.
one_line: Overview of Microsoft Windows' origins, from its 1983 announcement as a GUI for MS-DOS to its 1990s evolution into a full operating system.
key_facts: Microsoft Windows was announced by Bill Gates on November 10, 1983.
Microsoft introduced Windows as a graphical user interface for MS-DOS.
MS-DOS had been introduced a couple of years before Windows was announced.
In the 1990s, the Windows product line evolved from an operating environment into a fully complete, modern operating system.
The 1990s evolution took place over two lines of development.
Each of the two lines of Windows development had its own separate codebase.
